text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Soldier killed, another wounded in Lebanon.
- Israeli source says U.S. has stopped sharing intelligence on Iranian nuclear program out of fear of upsetting Russia.
- Retired Shin Bet secret service man who admitted role in deaths of two Palestinian guerrillas years ago informally asked to work with anti-terror head in prime minister's office.
- Hebron settler spokesman arrested after confrontation with police at Tomb of the Patriarchs.
- Sabbath "commando squad" of the Labour Ministry operates at weekend in Tel Aviv to ensure no one working illegal hours.
- Turkey approves deal with Israel Aircraft Industries on rehabilitating planes.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. seeks summit to ink Hebron pact.
- Religious parties incensed over arrest of Hebron settler spokesman on Jewish sabbath.
- Book: Peres offered to recognise Syrian sovereignty over Golan in 1992.
- Freud's birthplace, today part of Czech republic, now massage parlour.
MAARIV
- Today amount of additional budget cut to be revealed.
- Nixon on tapes just revealed, 'The rich Jews steal in every direction'.
- 55 percent of 9th to 12th graders think emigration is legitimate and it is the right of every person to decide where to live, says survey by Zionist Council.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Senior sources in Treasury: If no cut, more taxes.
- Analysis: Treasury has no great idea how to cut additional two billion shekels from 1997 budget; even the five billion shekel cut is still on lines of trial balloon.
- Israeli military acquisitions delegation in New York to be subjected to polygraph to see who takes or sells drugs after evidence found some were taking drugs.
- Assassinated prime minister Rabin's son visited Arafat in Gaza at the weekend.
